sampling_model.design: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent complete trajectories with common observed law equal to the observed margin of \(P\in\mathcal P_T\).
sampling_model.units: Each trajectory contains \(T\) binary covariates, \(T\) binary actions, and one terminal outcome in \([0,1]\).
sampling_model.treatment: At time \(t\), the unknown propensity \(\pi_t^P(H_t)\) may depend arbitrarily on the full observed past; deterministic actions and null histories are permitted.
sampling_model.overlap: No positive lower bound is imposed on \(\pi_t^P(H_t)\) or \(1-\pi_t^P(H_t)\); domination follows from the incremental kernel itself.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The analyst receives only \(n,T,c\), the alphabets, and the trajectories. The handle uses occupancy-adaptive polynomials of unconditional compatible prefix masses and nested-count factorial corrections; the oracle benchmark additionally supplies \(\Pi(P)\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The general identification model contains the present binary complete-case subclass after retention is fixed to one, but Theorem 6.1 instead assumes a common constant positive propensity; deterministic late propensities place the paired alternatives outside that special class, so only the present converse transfers upward to the general model and no result transfers to the Theorem 6.1 class.
The paper derives and attains local efficiency bounds for behavior-dependent tilting and modified-treatment policies under Markov or non-Markov policy models.
The paper develops one-stage switching, low-count polynomial, and behavior-mixture machinery for a fixed target policy, without nested longitudinal arms.
The paper proves discrete one-time causal minimax bounds driven by unseen contexts and within-cell collisions, without sequential parent-sum compatibility.
The paper characterizes a parametric fixed-policy history-length bias--variance tradeoff rather than an unrestricted minimax frontier.
CoinDICE constructs behavior-agnostic policy-value intervals from embedded Markov occupancy equations and proves asymptotic and nonasymptotic coverage statements.

body.tldr: The unknown-propensity problem has a proved, computable finite-history bracket and a matched long-history phase.  A truncated empirical prefix-trie estimator and a Markov-calibrated connected interval give explicit upper envelopes optimized over prefix depth, while complementary-context mixtures give explicit every-depth lower envelopes.  Once \(T\geq2\lceil\log_4(100n^2)\rceil\), these bounds match at \(R(n,T,c)\asymp\min\{1,n^{-1}+c^2\}\) and \(L(n,T,c)\asymp\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+c\}\); at \(c=0\) the rates are \(n^{-1}\) and \(n^{-1/2}\) for every \(T\).  The exact factor-two logarithmic elbow between full-prefix estimation near \(4^T\leq n\) and birthday-collision activation near \(4^k\geq100n^2\) remains open.

project_justification.gap: Kim, Kennedy, and Naimi derive identification, efficient influence functions, and nuisance-controlled fixed-horizon inference, but their growing-horizon theorem is a variance comparison under a common constant positive propensity.  Existing one-stage large-alphabet polynomial estimators and moment-matching converses do not enforce the parent-sum identities or nested-count covariance of a longitudinal history tree.  No inspected result closes the factor-two logarithmic elbow left between the proved truncated-tree upper envelope and the proved collision converse.
project_justification.niche: The centered finite-tree functional has a dimension-free local gradient, yet unrestricted unknown histories create a global sparse-context penalty.  The proved finite-depth bracket makes both sides computable on the original iid trajectory experiment and isolates the remaining issue: joint approximation of ancestor--descendant propensity ratios with a variance-matched factorial statistic and legal-subtree testing priors.
project_justification.fill: This note proves exact finite-tree identification, stable likelihood-ratio and local-gradient bounds, explicit finite-history upper and lower envelopes, total \(O(nT+T)\)-time prefix-trie procedures, the zero-shift endpoint, and the matched birthday-depth phase.  Constructing the unresolved polynomial or factorial correction with explicit degrees and coefficients, proving its nested-count second-moment bound, calibrating the corresponding sharper interval, constructing a matching legal-subtree converse, and evaluating the full intermediate optimization are future work rather than accomplished results.

body.related_work: Kim, Kennedy, and Naimi, \cite{KimKennedyNaimi2021}, Introduction, Theorems 3.1, 4.1, 5.1, and 6.1, and the concluding discussion, identify longitudinal incremental effects and develop fixed-horizon efficiency and nuisance-rate inference; their Theorem 6.1 instead compares variances under a common constant positive propensity.  The binary complete-case bounded-terminal-outcome class used here embeds as a subclass of their general identification model by taking every retention indicator to be one and filling unused intermediate outcomes, but it is neither their full published class nor their Theorem 6.1 class.  In particular, the paired alternatives here have deterministic late propensities.  Therefore a lower converse proved here transfers upward to their general model, an upper bound here remains restricted to the present binary complete-case class, and no result here transfers to their special Theorem 6.1 class.  Kennedy, \cite{Kennedy2019JASA}, supplies the support-respecting binary incremental functional and fixed-horizon efficiency theory.  Kallus and Uehara, \cite{KallusUehara2024NaturalPolicies}, derive local efficiency theory for behavior-dependent policies under additional policy-model structure.  Ma, Zhu, Jiao, and Wainwright, \cite{MaZhuJiaoWainwright2022}, and Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman, \cite{JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015}, provide one-stage low-count polynomial and factorial-moment methods, while Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, \cite{ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete}, analyze one-time discrete causal functionals.  None of those results supplies a joint approximation, covariance, and testing theorem for compatible nested prefixes.  Static-tilt results in \cite{SchindlShenKennedy2024} and \cite{HuangDongLinAntonelli2026} do not apply because Proposition~\ref{prop:static-nonreduction} rules out a single-normalizer reduction.  History-conditioned importance-sampling comparisons in \cite{ZhouHannaZhuYangShi2025} and \cite{LiuBaconBrunskill2020}, and Markov occupancy intervals in \cite{DaiEtAl2020CoinDICE}, impose structures absent from \(\mathcal P_T\).  Higher-order influence-function machinery in \cite{RobinsLiTchetgenVanderVaart2016TR} motivates factorial corrections but does not supply the missing tree-specific certificate.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The finite-history envelopes are rigorous but need not match in the intermediate region between full-prefix plug-in control near \(4^T\leq n\) and collision-converse activation near \(4^k\geq100n^2\).  Closing that factor-two logarithmic elbow requires explicit joint polynomial coefficients, a multinomial nested-count second-moment theorem, and dual priors supported on legal subtrees.  A scalar approximation or independent-Poisson prefix calculation cannot certify those requirements.  Thus no complete all-sequence consistency or oracle-penalty characterization is claimed outside the zero-shift and matched long-history regimes.
body.honest_scope: Identification is given.  The statistical model is the unrestricted binary, completely observed, bounded-terminal-outcome class, with no overlap floor, Markov property, smoothness, sparsity, or supplied nuisance kernel.  The finite-history bracket, total algorithms, long-history matched theorem, zero-shift reduction, oracle benchmark, and local-gradient bound are proved on this class, including deterministic actions and null histories.  This class embeds in the general Kim--Kennedy--Naimi identification model after retention is fixed to one, so its lower converses transfer upward, but its upper bounds do not establish results for that full model.  The deterministic late propensities also place the paired alternatives outside their Theorem 6.1 common-positive-propensity class, to which no result here is transferred.  The theory is not a numerical sample-size prescription for the richer EAGeR dropout analysis.
body.interpretation:
\section{Results at a glance}
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-history-envelopes} supplies explicit upper and lower functions for every \(n,T,c\), a total empirical prefix-trie estimator, and an honest connected interval.  Theorem~\ref{thm:long-history-frontier} shows that the functions match beyond the birthday-collision depth, despite uniformly bounded oracle weights and local efficient-influence-function norm.  Proposition~\ref{prop:endpoint-reduction} gives the ordinary bounded-mean rates at zero shift, and Proposition~\ref{prop:oracle-benchmark} gives the uniform oracle rates.  The two open questions now concern only the intermediate factor-two logarithmic elbow and its all-sequence consequences.
